intended_object: The A₂ quiver: two vertices 0 and 1 (Bourbaki numbering) with a single arrow 0 → 1, i.e. the A₂ Dynkin graph oriented from the smaller to the larger vertex. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation, which says "the orientation is from the smaller to the larger Bourbaki-numbered vertex". The module then forms the preprojective algebra of this quiver.
explanation:
`zigzagA2Graph` is the simple graph on `Fin 2` read off the A₂ Cartan matrix. Its adjacency is `i ≠ j` (lemma `zigzagA2Graph_adj`), so it has one edge between 0 and 1. `Orientation.ofLinearOrder` keeps exactly the darts with `fst < snd`, so it keeps only the dart 0 → 1. `OrientedQuiver G o` has the vertices of G, and its arrows i ⟶ j are adjacency proofs whose dart lies in the orientation. It is thin, so there is at most one arrow between any two vertices.

The result therefore has exactly one arrow, 0 → 1, and no others. The same file confirms this: it proves the Hom-types 0→0, 1→0 and 1→1 are empty and builds the unique arrow `preprojectiveA2Arrow : 0 ⟶ 1`.

This is the A₂ quiver with the orientation the docstring states. It is a specific object, so the "too narrow" criterion does not apply. Mathlib has no named A₂ quiver or general oriented-graph quiver construction to cite as a counterpart.
